metricsGlance.factsAboutNumbersWhat: . Facts about the numbers; what they mean is yours to judge.

summarySection.repositoryWasClonedDepth: The repository was cloned with --depth, so its history stops where the clone did: commit counts, contributors and ages cover only that
summarySection.howDependenciesWereFound: How the dependencies were found: an import names its target; a runtime lookup names it in a string; a type-only import is erased by the compiler and left out of coupling
summarySection.shallowCloneHistoryCut: shallow clone: history is cut short
summarySection.thoseFilesCommitsAverage: to those files, {value} commits on average
summarySection.componentsStronglyConnectedGroup: Components in a strongly connected group of two or more
summarySection.linesTangledComponentsOver: Lines of tangled components over all lines
summarySection.longestImportChainOnce: Longest import chain once tangles are collapsed
summarySection.committedDayScan: committed the day of the scan
summarySection.typesOnlyLeftOut: {typeOnly} types only, left out of coupling
summarySection.activeLatelySub: in the last 90 days of history

healthPanel.title: Code health
healthPanel.componentsNote: Mean health of their code, weighted by lines
healthPanel.filesNote: Code files of 100 lines or more

costs.one: {n} of {total} files carries half of the debt interest.
costs.other: {n} of {total} files carry half of the debt interest.

healthPanel.interestNote: Debt interest is bad code times how often it changes now. Code nobody touches costs nothing yet.

healthFigure.rowTitle: The code, and the effort of changing it
healthFigure.title: Code health: the code, and the effort of changing it
healthFigure.effortSentence: {share} of the change effort goes into unhealthy code.
healthFigure.effortNote: Change effort counts a file's lines once for every commit that changed it: a large file changed often costs the most.
healthFigure.legendScore: The number at the end of each bar is the average code health out of 10.

findings.title: Findings
findings.lede: Where to look first: the most out of the ordinary on top, each with what it rests on.
findings.none: Nothing stands out in this snapshot.
findings.shallowBody: The repository was cloned with --depth. Commits, contributors and ages cover only the history that was fetched.
findings.testsBody: {test} of tests against {production} lines of production code.

tanglesBody.one: {share} of the lines are in components that reach each other through imports, all in one tangle of {size} components.
tanglesBody.other: {share} of the lines are in components that reach each other through imports. The largest of {count} tangles holds {size} components.

findings.hotspotBody: {name} ({lines} lines) has {commits} and the highest hotspot score: it changes most, weighted by its size.
findings.concentrationTitle: One component holds much of the code
findings.concentrationBody: {component} holds {share} of the production code: {lines} lines in {files} files.

concentrationGenerated.one: Its largest file has at most two commits; code that large that never changes is usually generated.
concentrationGenerated.other: Its {count} largest files have at most two commits each; code that large that never changes is usually generated.

bigFilesBody.one: One code file is over 5,000 lines: {name}, at {lines} lines.
bigFilesBody.other: {count} code files are over 5,000 lines. The largest is {name}, at {lines} lines.

findings.hubTitle: Much of the code leans on one component
findings.hubBody: {component} is used by {count} components, {share} of all of them.
findings.hubUnstable: {component} is used by {count} components, {share} of all of them, yet depends on more than depends on it (instability {instability}).
findings.knowledgeTitle: Code that rests on one person

knowledgeBody.one: {share} of the production code is in one component where a single person added 90% or more of the lines.
knowledgeBody.other: {share} of the production code is in {count} components where a single person added 90% or more of the lines.

findings.arrivalBody: {share} of today's lines first appear on {date}, so their history before that day lives somewhere else.
findings.dormantTitle: History stops long before the scan
findings.dormantBody: The last commit is from {date}. Periods such as "the last 90 days" count back from it, not from the scan.
findings.recentTitle: Recent work is in one place
findings.recentBody: {component} took {share} of the {total} commits in the last 90 days of history.

rulesBody.one: One import breaks a module rule; it starts in {components}.
rulesBody.other: {count} imports break a module rule; most start in {components}.

findings.propagationBody: Through imports, a change in one component can reach {share} of the others on average.

zonePainBody.one: One component is concrete, stable and used by {floor} or more others. Every change to it reaches them all, and nothing abstract stands between.
zonePainBody.other: {count} components are concrete, stable and each used by {floor} or more others. Every change to them reaches all of those, and nothing abstract stands between.

zoneUselessBody.one: One component is mostly interfaces and abstract types, yet depends on more than depends on it. Abstractions nobody uses are cost without benefit.
zoneUselessBody.other: {count} components are mostly interfaces and abstract types, yet depend on more than depends on them. Abstractions nobody uses are cost without benefit.

architectureFindings.unstableDepsTitle: Stable code depends on volatile code

unstableDepsBody.one: One component that five or more others rely on depends on a far less stable one. When that one changes, the change travels up through everything built on top.
unstableDepsBody.other: {count} times a component that five or more others rely on depends on a far less stable one. When those change, the change travels up through everything built on top.

mutualBody.one: One pair of components imports each other directly. Neither can be changed, tested or moved without the other.
mutualBody.other: {count} pairs of components import each other directly. Neither side of a pair can be changed, tested or moved without the other.

architectureFindings.fanOutTitle: One component depends on very many
architectureFindings.fanOutBody: {component} depends on {count} components, {share} of all of them. It has to change whenever any of them does.
architectureFindings.bottleneckTitle: Most dependency paths run through one component
architectureFindings.bottleneckBody: {component} sits on {share} of the shortest paths between other components. A change there travels furthest.

orphansBody.one: One component is imported by nothing and declares no entry point: dead code, or reached only by framework wiring.
orphansBody.other: {count} components, {share} of the production code, are imported by nothing and declare no entry point: dead code, or reached only by framework wiring.

architectureFindings.moduleCyclesTitle: Build modules depend on each other in a circle

moduleCyclesBody.one: One circle of {size} build modules, among them {modules}. They can only be built and released together.
moduleCyclesBody.other: {count} circles of build modules; the largest holds {size}, among them {modules}. Modules in a circle can only be built and released together.

architectureFindings.hiddenTitle: Change together without importing each other

hiddenBody.one: One pair of components changes in the same commits without either importing the other: {a} and {b}, {shared} commits together. Something ties them the code does not show.
hiddenBody.other: {count} pairs of components change in the same commits without either importing the other. {a} and {b} changed together {shared} times. Something ties them the code does not show: a shared format, a database table, a copy.

architectureFindings.shotgunBody: {share} of the commits, {wide} of {commits}, touch five components or more. One change that must be made in many places means the parts are not cut along the lines the work runs.
architectureFindings.abandonedTitle: Code whose main author has gone

abandonedBody.one: In one component the person who wrote most of it has made no commit in the last year of history.
abandonedBody.other: In {count} components, {share} of the production code, the person who wrote most of it has made no commit in the last year of history.

architectureFindings.frozenTitle: Code that has not changed in two years
architectureFindings.frozenBody: {share} of the production code has not changed in the two years before the last commit. Stable, or avoided; either way nobody has it fresh in mind.
architectureFindings.growthBody: {component} grew by {lines} lines in the last 180 days of history, {share} of all growth.

complexBody.one: One function scores 25 or more for cognitive complexity.
complexBody.other: {count} of {total} functions score 25 or more for cognitive complexity; {top} of them sit in just five files.

longBody.one: One function is 150 lines or longer: several jobs in one place.
longBody.other: {count} functions are 150 lines or longer: several jobs in one place, hard to test on their own.

architectureFindings.vendoredBody: {share} of all lines, {lines}, is vendored third-party code. It ages without updates and inflates every count that does not leave it out.
architectureFindings.generatedBody: {share} of all lines, {lines}, is generated. Reviews and diffs read it as if someone wrote it.
architectureFindings.sameNamesTitle: The same type name in many components

sameNamesBody.one: One type name is declared in three components or more.
sameNamesBody.other: {count} type names are declared in three components or more; {name} in {components}. Copies of one idea, or an idea with no home.

entitiesBody.one: {entity} is read or written by {components} components. They are coupled through the database, whatever the imports say.
entitiesBody.other: {entity} is read or written by {components} components, and {count} entities by three or more. Components that share tables are coupled through the database, whatever the imports say.

architectureFindings.endpointsDataTitle: Endpoints that go straight to the database

endpointsDataBody.one: One component serves HTTP and reads or writes the database itself, with no layer in between.
endpointsDataBody.other: {count} components serve HTTP and read or write the database themselves, with no layer in between.

architectureFindings.outboundUnprotectedTitle: Outside calls with no visible protection
architectureFindings.outboundUnprotectedBody: {calls} calls to {systems} outside systems from {components} components, and the scan found no retry, timeout or circuit breaker on any of them.
architectureFindings.outboundBody: {calls} calls to {systems} outside systems, made from {components} components.
architectureFindings.openEndpointsTitle: Endpoints with no visible access control
architectureFindings.openEndpointsAll: None of the {count} HTTP endpoints declares access control in code. It may sit in a filter or a gateway; check that it does.
architectureFindings.openEndpointsBody: {open} of {count} HTTP endpoints declare no access control in code.
architectureFindings.undocumentedBody: Only {documented} of {count} HTTP endpoints carry documentation the scan could find.

unitsGlance.lanesFloorsReferencesBetween: The lanes as floors, with the references between them
unitsGlance.stackedSoMostReferences: Stacked so most references run down; red runs back against the grain. Click a lane or a link to open what it is made of.
unitsGlance.referencesBetweenModulesWere: References between modules were not resolved in this snapshot, so no lane can be read against another.
unitsGlance.noReferencesCrossLane: No references cross a lane boundary in this snapshot.
unitsGlance.nothingStandsOutSnapshot: Nothing stands out in this snapshot. Every module sits on its own.
